compiled_state.title: RED: ProvenanceLedger module with record/is_echo/to_dict
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Story DD Coverage
- dd-3: provenance {side, timestamp} per element; serializable; unit test asserts both fields present

## Testing Mode
RED

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Unit tests pass (exit 0)
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_provenance_ledger.py
- [ ] Lint passes (exit 0)
  Verify: make lint-ruff
- [ ] Format check passes (exit 0)
  Verify: make format-check
- [ ] ProvenanceLedger.record writes an entry whose to_dict() output exposes 'side' and 'timestamp' keys per element
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_provenance_ledger.py::test_record_exposes_side_and_timestamp
- [ ] ProvenanceLedger.is_echo returns True for content-hash-identical values without consulting record() history (stateless content-equality)
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_provenance_ledger.py::test_is_echo_is_stateless_content_equality
- [ ] to_dict() output is JSON-serializable via json.dumps() with no TypeError
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_provenance_ledger.py::test_to_dict_is_json_serializable

## Implementation Notes
Create plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/provenance_ledger.py defining ProvenanceLedger dataclass:

- record(element_class: str, element_id: str, side: str, timestamp: str, content_hash: str) -> None — appends an entry. Use param name 'side' (NOT 'origin') to align with dd-3 wording verbatim.
- is_echo(element_class: str, element_id: str, local_value, jira_value) -> bool — returns True iff content_hash(local_value) == content_hash(jira_value). MUST NOT consult prior record() entries. Hash via sha256 over canonical json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, default=str).
- to_dict() -> dict — keyed by (element_class, element_id); each entry contains 'side' and 'timestamp' keys verbatim per dd-3.

Lives one pass: instantiated by differ at pass start, discarded at end. Stateless content-equality means is_echo is a pure function of (local_value, jira_value) — no instance state read.

## Retry Budget
MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model)
On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages)
On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history
If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately

comments.body:
AC amendment (gap-analysis): Specify element_id extraction rule per class. is_echo(element_class, element_id, local_value, jira_value) requires a stable id per class. Pin a docstring table in provenance_ledger.py mapping:
- state scalars (status/assignee/priority/title/type/description as scalar): element_id = field name (string); only one entry per field per pass.
- comments (additive): element_id = Jira comment id when present, else sha256(body) — comments authored locally pre-roundtrip have no Jira id, use body-hash as stable surrogate.
- labels (set): element_id = the label string itself (degenerate but unambiguous; dedup via set semantics).
- watchers (set): element_id = account id (preferred) or display name (fallback).
- links (set): element_id = composite f'{link_type}:{target_key}'.
Add a unit test per class asserting the rule. Without this, T3 sub-agent + T4 fixture author will pick inconsistent conventions → false positives/negatives.

comments.body:
AC amendment (gap-analysis): Hash canonicalization MUST strip volatile fields per element class before hashing. Jira returns 'created', 'updated', 'updateAuthor', 'self' (URL) on comments and 'self' on links — these change on no-op roundtrips and would defeat is_echo. Define a per-class volatile-field allowlist in provenance_ledger.py:
- comments: drop {'created','updated','updateAuthor','self','id'} before hashing the body
- links: drop {'self','id'}
- watchers/labels/scalars: pass through (no volatile fields)
Add unit test: comment with identical body but different 'updated' timestamps → is_echo returns True.
